paper_title: Dark Matter Axion Search with HAYSTAC Phase II
notes: HAYSTAC Phase II (IIc/d) reports exclusion limits on axion-photon coupling |g_γ| expressed as multiples of the KSVZ benchmark value |g_γ^KSVZ| = -0.97. Three distinct exclusion regions are reported: (1) Phase IIc (17.28–18.44 µeV): |g_γ| ≥ 2.75×|g_γ^KSVZ|; (2) Phase IId (18.71–19.46 µeV): |g_γ| ≥ 2.96×|g_γ^KSVZ|; (3) Combined Phase II (16.96–19.46 µeV): |g_γ| ≥ 2.86×|g_γ^KSVZ|. The coupling values are dimensionless ratios to KSVZ. To convert to absolute g_γ in GeV^-1, multiply by |g_γ^KSVZ| ≈ 0.97 × 10^-10 GeV^-1 (standard KSVZ value). Data points encode the mass ranges and corresponding coupling limits at 90% CL. Local DM density ρ_a = 0.45 GeV/cm³ is explicitly stated in the signal power formula. The experiment uses a squeezed state receiver to achieve sub-quantum-limited noise and demonstrates a scan rate enhancement E ≈ 1.7 relative to quantum-limited operation. No axion signal was detected; 12 RFI candidates were identified and vetoed.
